subject: Novaparts: intermittent supplier portal login loops behind corporate proxy

Subject: Re: [URGENT] Supplier portal sign-in looping for some of our vendors

Hi Camila,

We're still seeing the sign-in loop for ~12 of our vendors: they enter credentials, get redirected to the portal, and immediately land back at the same login page (no error). This started after our security team deployed a new web proxy rule (Netskope/Zscaler).

Attached I've included a screenshot and the network capture the vendors sent (sso-trace-headers.txt). The vendors are mostly on corporate-managed laptops. From our IT team: they see 200 OK responses for the POST but the portal never sets the session cookie in the browser.

Can Redwood confirm whether anything changed on your side that would cause POST responses to be cached or for Set-Cookie to be dropped? Our vendors can access the portal when they go through personal networks, so we suspect the proxy.

Elena Morales
Accounts Payable Lead, Novaparts

Subject: Re: [URGENT] Supplier portal sign-in looping for some of our vendors

Hi Elena — thanks for the quick report and the traces. I pulled the files into our shared folder and started a triage with Engineering. Initial read of the trace shows a proxy sitting between vendor and our portal that is rewriting cache headers and, crucially, returning cached responses to the POST /auth/login endpoint. That would explain a missing Set-Cookie reaching the browser.

Immediate asks: 
- Can Novaparts IT whitelist the portal origin (portal.redwood.com) and the /auth/login and /sso/* endpoints from response caching? A quick test is to disable caching rules for those host/path combos.
- In parallel, engineering will verify our responses include Cache-Control: no-store and Vary headers, and that Set-Cookie is delivered on the redirect chain.

I'll loop in Ben and Laura for commercial visibility. If we need, we can produce a short runbook you can share with vendor IT teams.

Action: engineering ticket INF-11983 created (internal). ETA for a first engineering reply is 2 hours.

Best,
Camila Reyes

From: Platform Infra <infra@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Feb 2027 13:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: INF-11983 — POST caching via intermediate proxy causing lost Set-Cookie on /auth/login (Novaparts)

Hi team,

We investigated INF-11983. Findings: our /auth/login POST returns a 302 -> GET redirect flow and we already send Set-Cookie on the 302. Responses include "Cache-Control: no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate" and "Pragma: no-cache". However, the proxy in the attached trace (company edge appliance) is rewriting the 302 response and serving a cached 200 HTML snapshot for subsequent requests. The proxy appears to be caching the POST redirect chain because the response lacked a Vary header that would tell the proxy to consider Authorization/Cookie.

Remediation steps (we will deploy a change in the next 1 hour):
1) Add "Vary: Cookie, Authorization" on auth endpoints and redirect responses. This prevents many aggressive proxies from serving a cached redirect.
2) Harden headers: add "Cache-Control: private, no-store" on the 302 response and ensure Set-Cookie uses SameSite=None; Secure; HttpOnly.
3) Publish a short runbook for customer IT: whitelist portal.redwood.com and ensure their proxy does not cache responses with Set-Cookie. Include sample proxy rules for Zscaler and Netskope.

Temporary mitigation for Novaparts: we can generate one-time activation links for affected vendors that bypass the redirect flow (signed URL with single-use token). I have generated two test links and shared them to Camila via secure chat. If OK, Camila can distribute them to the 12 affected vendors.

I'll update INF-11983 when the change is deployed (target 14:30 PST).

— Platform Infra (SRE)
infra@redwood.com

---
Notes: please ensure Novaparts IT also restarts any proxy cache after whitelisting; cached snapshots may persist for default TTLs.
